564  def allocate_kv_cache(
 565      kv_cache_config: KVCacheConfig,
 566      device: torch.device,
 567      layout: KVCacheLayout,
 568      kernel_block_sizes: list[int] | None = None,
 569  ) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
 570      """Allocate the KV cache and view it as ``[B, H, N, C]`` per layer.
 571  
 572      Every KVCacheTensor places its layers in the same backing allocation: layer ``l`` of
 573      block ``b`` starts at ``offset + l * layer_stride + b * block_stride``. Cache
 574      groups overlay each other, so tensors may address the same bytes.
 575      """
 576      if not kv_cache_config.kv_cache_tensors:
 577          return {}
 578  
 579      sizes = {tensor.size for tensor in kv_cache_config.kv_cache_tensors}
 580      assert len(sizes) == 1, "KV cache tensors must share one backing allocation."
 581      raw_size = sizes.pop()
 582      # wvSplitKrc's process-lifetime static workspaces (csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms.cu)
 583      # are created lazily on the first qualifying GEMM. Force that now, before
 584      # the giant backing allocation below: if one landed in this segment's
 585      # rounding tail it would pin the whole segment at engine shutdown.
 586      if current_platform.is_rocm():
 587          warmup_rocm_skinny_gemm_workspaces(device)
 588          # Pad to the page granularity MoRIIO needs to register the shared
 589          # backing as a single RDMA memory region. Other platforms keep the
 590          # exact-size allocation (see #53974), so anything reading
 591          # storage.nbytes() has to tolerate the tail on ROCm alone.
 592          page_size = 4096
 593          buf_size = ((raw_size + page_size - 1) // page_size) * page_size
 594      else:
 595          buf_size = raw_size
 596      buf = torch.zeros(buf_size, dtype=torch.int8, device=device)
 597  
 598      kv_caches: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}
 599      for tensor in kv_cache_config.kv_cache_tensors:
 600          layer_name = tensor.layers[0]

 678          self.current_step += 1
 679          # NOTE(woosuk) on the scheduling algorithm:
 680          # There's no "decoding phase" nor "prefill phase" in the scheduler.
 681          # Each request just has the num_computed_tokens and
 682          # num_tokens_with_spec. num_tokens_with_spec =
 683          # len(prompt_token_ids) + len(output_token_ids) + len(spec_token_ids).
 684          # At each step, the scheduler tries to assign tokens to the requests
 685          # so that each request's num_computed_tokens can catch up its
 686          # num_tokens_with_spec. This is general enough to cover
 687          # chunked prefills, prefix caching, speculative decoding,

free.code:
776      def free_blocks(self, ordered_blocks: Iterable[KVCacheBlock]) -> None:
 777          """Free a list of blocks. The blocks should be ordered by their
 778          eviction priority, where the first block will be evicted first.
 779  
 780          Args:
 781              ordered_blocks: A list of blocks to free ordered by their eviction
 782                  priority.
 783  
 784          """
 785          # Identify blocks with hash (LRU cache) and without it (never match APC)
 786          blocks_to_evict_last = []
 787          blocks_to_evict_first = []
 788          other_pools: dict[BlockPool, list[KVCacheBlock]] = {}
 789          for block in ordered_blocks:
 790              if block.is_null:  # never pooled; its ref_cnt is not maintained
 791                  continue
 792              if block.pool is not None and block.pool is not self:
 793                  other_pools.setdefault(block.pool, []).append(block)
 794                  continue
 795              block.ref_cnt -= 1
 796              if block.ref_cnt == 0:
 797                  if block.block_hash is None or not self.enable_caching:
 798                      # LIFO reuse of non-cached blocks for better GPU locality.
 799                      blocks_to_evict_first.append(block)
 800                  else:
 801                      # FIFO reuse of cached blocks for LRU eviction behavior.
 802                      blocks_to_evict_last.append(block)
 803  
 804          # Blocks to reuse first are prepended to the front of the free queue.
 805          self.free_block_queue.prepend_n(blocks_to_evict_first)
 806          # Blocks to reuse last are appended to the end of the free queue.
 807          self.free_block_queue.append_n(blocks_to_evict_last)
 808          for pool, blocks in other_pools.items():
 809              pool.free_blocks(blocks)
 810
